local_meaning.text: Fire can start and spread quickly in dry, windy weather. Don't burn outdoors, and avoid anything that throws sparks. Know your way out and keep your phone charged.
Visibility on the road can drop to nearly zero without warning. If caught driving, pull off the road, turn off your lights, take your foot off the brake, and wait it out. Stay indoors if you can.
Dangerous heat. Check on older neighbors and anyone without air conditioning, drink water steadily, and take breaks indoors. Never leave people or pets in a parked car.
Dry washes and low road crossings can fill in minutes, even if it isn't raining where you are. Never drive or walk through moving water, and move to higher ground.
Strong gusts can drop limbs onto power lines, so outages are possible. Secure trash cans, outdoor furniture, and anything that can blow away. Take extra care in a high-sided vehicle.
Roads may be slow to clear, so plan to stay put. Stock up before it starts, keep the fuel tank full, and arrange backup power if you rely on medical equipment.
Go to the lowest floor, an interior room, away from windows, now.
Brief but violent wind and lightning. Get indoors and away from windows. Unplug sensitive electronics.
